old: Procedure: split by what the expression names, not by whether it is true. A boundary probe calls, inside a requires-expression, a production function declared outside the probed type's own header (a kernel, a free function, a member of another class). Keep it. A shape check names only the probed type: a type trait, sizeof, alignof, or a requires-expression whose body calls only the probed type's own members or their absence (an accessor on a temporary, a write through at(), a missing operator). For each shape check: (a) search `h/` for the same trait on the same type or on an enclosing type that holds it as a member, resolving aliases; (b) check whether the probed type's own declaration already fixes the trait (alignas, `= delete`, an array member). Either one makes the check a repeat.
new:
Procedure: split by what the expression names, not by whether it is true.

- A boundary probe calls, inside a requires-expression (the C++20 construct that tests whether an expression compiles), a production function declared outside the probed type's own header (a kernel, a free function, a member of another class). Keep it.
- A shape check names only the probed type: a type trait, sizeof, alignof, or a requires-expression whose body calls only the probed type's own members or their absence (an accessor on a temporary, a write through at(), a missing operator).
- For each shape check: (a) search `h/` for the same trait on the same type or on an enclosing type that holds it as a member, resolving aliases; (b) check whether the probed type's own declaration already fixes the trait (alignas, `= delete`, an array member). Either one makes the check a repeat.

old: - a trait production code relies on that no declaration or header fixes.
new: - a trait that production code relies on, and that no declaration or header fixes.

old: a formula written out in the test, and between the start of the TEST_CASE and that assertion stands a runtime exit (`return`, SKIP, WARN plus return) conditioned on a hardware or environment probe (`available()`, a cpuinfo flag, FPGA presence, getenv). Test selection labels in t/CMakeLists.txt (min_slices_N) are a separate gate; list them under selection.
new: a formula written out in the test. Between the start of the TEST_CASE and that assertion stands a runtime exit (`return`, SKIP, WARN plus return, where SKIP and WARN are Catch2 macros) conditioned on a hardware or environment probe (`available()`, a cpuinfo flag, FPGA presence, getenv). Test selection labels in t/CMakeLists.txt (min_slices_N) are a separate gate. List them under selection.

old: Procedure: record every early exit above the assertion and its condition. Check whether any statement between the exit and the assertion executes the probed instructions (for `available()`: a call into the AMX kernel namespace; AVX-512 intrinsics do not count, every runner has them). For each lane that can run the binary, record its trigger and whether its configure line sets the build flag the TEST_CASE needs; on a lane where the flag is off the whole case is compiled out. On a lane where it is on, check whether every runner the job can land on passes the probe (README.ci.md runner table). Find the oracle of the assertion. If a production accessor of the same storage produces the expected side, both sides share the helper. List every other non-gated assertion on the same storage and classify it: an independent formula substitutes; a route check through the same helper never does; a second reader with its own address arithmetic substitutes only when it covers both parities and a pair beyond the first.
new:
Procedure:
1. Record every early exit above the assertion and its condition.
2. Check whether any statement between the exit and the assertion executes the probed instructions. For `available()` that means a call into the AMX kernel namespace. AVX-512 (the vector instruction set every runner has) intrinsics do not count.
3. For each lane that can run the binary, record its trigger and whether its configure line sets the build flag the TEST_CASE needs. On a lane where the flag is off, the whole case is compiled out.
4. On a lane where the flag is on, check whether every runner the job can land on passes the probe (README.ci.md runner table).
5. Find the oracle of the assertion. If a production accessor of the same storage produces the expected side, both sides share the helper.
6. List every other non-gated assertion on the same storage and classify it. An independent formula substitutes. A route check through the same helper never does. A second reader with its own address arithmetic substitutes only when it covers both parities and a pair beyond the first.

old: Four separate facts, each stated: the target compiles on the lane; the test case is selected; the assertion is reachable on the runner; a log shows the path executed. If runner capability or a log is unavailable, write `Insufficient data` and name it.
new: State four separate facts: (1) the target compiles on the lane, (2) the test case is selected, (3) the assertion is reachable on the runner, (4) a log shows the path executed. If runner capability or a log is unavailable, write `Insufficient data` and name it.
